newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up on end-of-week book squaring.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up on end-of-week book squaring.

text.p: July Brent crude futures were higher in late afternoon trading on Friday, taking their cue from higher NYMEX futures which have gained from end-of-week book squaring.
July Brent, trading on SIMEX, was last traded at $18.43 per barrel, reclaiming 11 cents of London's overnight 40-cent loss.
August was last traded at $18.63, up 17 cents from London.
NYMEX July crude was last traded on ACCESS at $19.77 per barrel, up 11 cents from New York.

Brokers said that players were squaring some positions ahead of the weekend after this week's sharp losses. However, they said the outlook for next week remained weak amid ample supplies on both sides of the Atlantic.

Brokers said data from the International Energy Agency (IEA) did not offer any immediate leads for the market, although offered some background support because of forecasts of moderate supply tightness raising the call on OPEC oil.
